name: Fingrid: signed data-centre connection agreements

source.access: Public press release / PDF, free

classification_rationale: Signed agreements carry financial commitment and are backed by multi-year hyperscaler programmes; they do not reverse with a quarterly capex cycle. Conversion to energised load is uncertain in timing, not in direction.

value.label: signed DC connection capacity unchanged for two quarters; two projects withdrawn

excerpt: [DEMODATA, world situation 2] Signed data-centre connection capacity remained at 3.0 GW for the second consecutive quarter; two agreements in Southern Finland were withdrawn.

usage_restrictions: Public; cite Fingrid. Project-level details not disclosed.

name: Fingrid: data-centre connection inquiries in the queue
lead_months_rationale: [ASSUMPTION: inquiries precede agreements by 6-18 months and energisation by 3-5 years; most inquiries never convert.]

source.name: [DEMODATA, world situation 2] Borenius legal alert: Government prepares new grid connection priority rules; DCD report
source.access: Public web article

classification_rationale: Inquiries are cheap options, not commitments. A queue of ~24 GW against a country peak load of roughly 15 GW is speculative by construction and behaves like double-ordering: the same developer files in several places.

value.label: connection inquiries down from 24 GW after speculative applications were withdrawn

excerpt: [DEMODATA, world situation 2] Connection inquiries fell to about 15 GW as speculative applications were withdrawn ahead of the new priority rules.
history_note: Only the August 2026 point (~24 GW) is from the source.
usage_restrictions: Secondary reporting of Fingrid figures; confirm against Fingrid primary data before use in internal planning.

name: European core-market grid moratoria and connection queues (FLAP-D, Denmark)
